## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.
4. Extend SettingsRecord with musicVolume/musicMuted and route them independently of SFX.
5. Add unit tests for each acceptance criterion.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by Music contract mapping and traceability guard (AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3), which is itself blocked by the chapter docs item (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W).
- Reuses the shared AudioContext and provider seam in src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts.

## Risky assumption

Baked stems (not runtime synthesis) are the delivery mechanism, consistent with the shipped ToneForge pipeline; recorded as an assumption in the parent item's plan.

**Key Files:**
- src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (new)
- src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts (new)
- src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts (shared AudioContext/provider seam to reuse)
- src/scenes/MenuScene.ts (gesture + menu/attract wiring)
- src/core/settingsStore.ts (music volume/mute)
- audio/toneforge/manifest.json (stem entry)
- scripts/build-audio.sh (bake pipeline)

# Checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 1 (interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests).

## Goal

As a **developer recording a long human session**, when I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured saved to a documented partial file, so an hour of play is not lost outright.

The run lives only in the page's in-memory buffer (`window.__aiHellTelemetry`); today `main()` drains it to disk once, after the wait loop, so a closed page has nothing to read. Checkpoint the buffer incrementally to `<output>.partial.jsonl` while recording and finalise that partial as the salvaged session when the page dies.

## Scope

- Resolve the recording output path (`resolveRecordingOutputPath`) **before** the browser launches, so the partial path exists at crash time; the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp becomes the **start** time.
- Add `--checkpoint-ms MS` (default `15000`, `0` disables) to `parseRecordArgs`, the flag table and the `--help` block.
- Checkpoint writer: on each interval, read **only new bytes** via the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop (reuse the seam; never a whole-buffer single CDP message — AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH), append only up to the last newline (never a half-written record; carry the remainder into the next read), and restart from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`).
- On a `target_closed` stop, finalise the partial as the salvaged session: collision-safe name (numeric suffix) so a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (mirror the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage), print **one** actionable line naming the partial path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure, exit 1. Do **not** write `balance-stats.json` for a salvaged partial.
- On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`): write the final file exactly as today, remove the partial, write `balance-stats.json` as today, exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; the process exits non-zero. The checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing), and a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording — both proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, the exit code is unchanged, and no `balance-stats.json` is written for a salvaged partial.
2. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves the checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing).
3. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (collision-safe numeric suffix).
4. `--checkpoint-ms` (default 15000, `0` disables) is parsed, covered by `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` argument-parsing assertions, and passed through to the checkpoint writer.
5. The checkpoint appends only new bytes through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop — no per-tick full re-read of the buffer, no unbounded in-process buffering — and every written line parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl`.
6. A salvaged partial and its message are additive: the clean-path success output, `balance-stats.json` and exit code are exactly as today.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — output path resolved up front, `--checkpoint-ms`, checkpoint writer, salvage finaliser, stop-reason handling.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — checkpoint append/reset and no-overwrite tests.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — declarations for new exports and the `checkpointMs` option.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (reused, not modified).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — flag row added to the table (prose/behaviour documented in child 3).

## Notes

- Recordings and partials stay under the gitignored `recordings/`; tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs.
- Long-run cost risk: one CDP round-trip plus a small append per interval; the final read still uses the existing whole-buffer chunked reader. Measurement is child 4.
- This child extends child 1's single rescue seam with the partial-writing branch; it does not add a second failure path.
- If AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD (page → dev-server streaming) ships first, this local checkpoint becomes redundant and the salvage message should point at the server-side partial — a follow-up, not part of this child.
data.title: Checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage

# Recorder stop procedure in usage text and docs

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 2 (checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage) — the docs must describe the behaviour that actually ships.

## Goal

As a **developer reading the tooling**, I want `npm run record --help` and the recording docs to state the stop procedure (Ctrl+C saves; closing the window does not save a completed recording) and the correct `--auto` invocation, so the mistake is avoidable in the first place.

## Scope

- `scripts/record-session.mjs` `--help` text: press Ctrl+C in the terminal to finish and save; closing the browser window ends the recording and at best salvages a partial file; `--auto` must be passed after `--` (`npm run record -- --auto`); list `--checkpoint-ms`.
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`: extend the existing `--help`/usage assertions to pin the new lines (spawned-CLI assertion as today).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1: flag table row for `--checkpoint-ms`, and rewrite the Ctrl+C paragraph — the existing claim that "on Ctrl+C the tool still exports whatever the sink has already flushed … so an interrupted run yields a partial but valid recording" must state the partial-path and partial-vs-final semantics, the salvage/lost behaviour and the stop procedure.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`: the recorder paragraphs (buffer-read description) must name the partial path, the checkpoint flag, the salvage/lost behaviour and the stop procedure.
- Any README or code-comment text that describes the recorder's stop behaviour is updated to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Usage text and docs state the stop requirement.** `npm run record --help` (and `node scripts/record-session.mjs --help`) states the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement, that closing the browser window does not save a completed recording (at best a partial), and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form; asserted by a test on the help output.
2. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table + the Ctrl+C paragraph) documents the partial path, partial-vs-final semantics, the salvage/lost behaviour, the `--checkpoint-ms` flag and the stop procedure.
3. The recorder paragraphs in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` document the same partial path, `--checkpoint-ms` flag, salvage/lost behaviour and stop procedure.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries; no doc still claims an interrupted run always yields a valid complete recording.
5. `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` asserts the new usage lines and keeps the existing argument-parsing assertions passing.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `--help` block.
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` — usage/help assertions.
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 — flag table and Ctrl+C paragraph.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` — recorder buffer-read / dev-tooling paragraphs.
- `./README.md` — only if it describes the recorder's stop behaviour.

## Notes

- Docs describe shipped behaviour only — this child lands after child 2, and must not document speculative flags.
- No repository-boundary edits (`.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`).

# Real-browser salvage verification and checkpoint cost check

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 2 (checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage), child 3 (usage text and docs).

## Goal

As a **maintainer**, I want end-to-end evidence that a real browser close mid-recording salvages a usable partial (not just a mocked one), that the checkpoint interval's CDP + append cost is acceptable on a long run, and that the clean path is still byte-identical — so the stringly target-closed detection and the checkpoint interval default are validated against reality rather than assumed.

## Scope

- Drive a real (headless is fine) recording through `scripts/record-session.mjs` (or the shipped `npm run record`), close the browser mid-recording, and confirm: one actionable first line naming the partial path, exit code 1, and a partial file whose every line parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`.
- Confirm the lost-message branch end-to-end (browser closed before any checkpoint, e.g. `--checkpoint-ms` larger than the run duration or with no telemetry read possible).
- Measure the checkpoint cost on a long run (30-minute budget or a scaled equivalent with a documented extrapolation): CDP round-trips and bytes appended per interval, peak RSS, and the final whole-buffer read; record whether `--checkpoint-ms 15000` stays the default.
- Verify clean-path parity: a Ctrl+C / `--auto` recording produces byte-identical output to the pre-change recorder (compare against a recording made on the parent commit) and no partial file remains.
- Record all evidence (commands, timings, exit codes, file sizes, sample first line) as comments on this work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** The dev-push gate's full suite runs green, including `scripts/record-session.test.ts` and `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`.
2. A real-browser interruption run (browser closed mid-recording) salvages a partial file that parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`, prints one actionable first line naming that path and the Ctrl+C procedure, and exits non-zero — evidence recorded on this work item.
3. A real-browser run closed before any checkpoint captures nothing, prints exactly one actionable line naming the resolved output path that was not written and the Ctrl+C procedure, and exits non-zero — evidence recorded on this work item.
4. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to the pre-change recorder's output for the same seed, no partial file remains, `balance-stats.json` is still written and the exit code is unchanged — evidence recorded on this work item.
5. Checkpoint cost for a long run (30-minute budget or a documented scaled equivalent) is measured and recorded — CDP round-trips per interval, bytes appended, peak RSS — with the `--checkpoint-ms` default confirmed or a tuned default proposed on this work item.
6. Any risk or divergence found (target-closed error-shape differences across Playwright surfaces, checkpoint cost, leftover partials) is recorded as a comment, and a `discovered-from:AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ` work item is created for anything out of scope.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — the tool under verification (no changes expected unless a measurement shows the default needs tuning).
- `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`, `scripts/recording.mjs` — `parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording` used to validate the salvaged partial.
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — flag default and stop procedure confirmed against the measured behaviour.

## Notes

- Long-running commands here follow the shared background-job etiquette (launch → prepare → one completion-aware wait via `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` → collect).
- All agent test runs go through the test skill (`/skill:test`); the full-suite gate is the dev-push hook.
- Recordings written during verification stay under the gitignored `recordings/`; nothing tracked is dirtied.

## Goal

Measure where the frame time actually goes at 100 late-game enemies, record the current baseline, and turn the profile into a ranked, evidence-based optimisation backlog.

**User story:** As a developer, I want a CPU profile and a recorded baseline for the 100-enemy scenario, so I know which hot spots are worth fixing and in what order — instead of guessing.

## Why

The parent item is a **proactive** optimisation pass with **no existing profiling** (producer answers 1–2), and the brief's structural suspects (allocations, collision passes, per-frame `Graphics` redraws) are unmeasured. The parent's AC6 requires every optimisation to cite profiler evidence and before/after numbers. This child produces that evidence and sets priorities for the structural children.

## Scope

- Run the frame-time harness (sibling child) against `GymPerformance` (sibling child) and `PlayScene` late game.
- Capture a **CPU profile** via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`Profiler.start`/`Profiler.stop`) during a sustained 100-enemy run, on desktop browser and the packaged Electron app; under a CPU throttle for the mobile tier.
- Attribute frame time across coarse buckets: JS simulation (movement/fire/collision/drops), renderer draw submission, GC/allocation, audio, telemetry, idle.
- Record a **baseline table** in the work item and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`: per-bucket ms, p50/p95/max frame time, FPS, long-frame counts, platform, throttle factor, reference-machine description, commit hash.
- Produce a **ranked hotspot list** with source locations (`file:line`), each with measured share and an estimated win. File or update optimisation child items from that list and **set their priorities by measured impact** — including re-ranking the pre-created structural children (broad-phase collision, per-frame allocations, GPU offload/draw-call batching).
- Determine whether the loop is genuinely CPU-bound or renderer/GPU-bound, and state that conclusion explicitly (the parent's premise "assuming we are CPU bound" must be confirmed or refuted).

## Out of scope

- Implementing any optimisation (children created here do that).
- Changing gameplay behaviour, waves or balance.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A CPU profile for a sustained 100-enemy run is captured and stored/linked (artifact path recorded), on desktop browser and Electron, plus a CPU-throttled mobile-tier run.
2. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` contains the baseline table with p50/p95/max frame time, effective FPS, long-frame counts, per-bucket attribution, platform, throttle factor, reference-machine description and commit hash.
3. A ranked hotspot list with `file:line` locations and measured share of frame time is recorded as a comment on this item and in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
4. The CPU-bound vs renderer-bound question is answered with evidence, and the answer is recorded on the parent work item.
5. Optimisation child items exist for the measured hotspots (creating them if the pre-provisioned structural children do not cover a hotspot), each carrying its measured impact, and their `priority` values are set from that impact — not from speculation.
6. Re-running the harness after no code change reproduces the baseline within the harness noise floor, confirming the baseline is trustworthy.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- **Parent AC trace — parent AC3.** **Baseline recorded.** A baseline measurement from the current `main` is captured on desktop browser and Electron with the stress gym at 100 enemies, and the numbers are recorded in the work item and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. This baseline is the "before" number every optimisation child must beat. *(Traces to parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC3; this item is where it is satisfied.)*
- **Parent AC trace — parent AC6.** **Evidence-driven changes.** Every optimisation child records the profiler evidence (hotspot, share of frame time, source location) that justifies it and the before/after harness numbers. Hotspots found during profiling become child work items, prioritised by measured impact — not by speculation. *(Traces to parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC6; this item is where it is satisfied.)*

# Weapon catalogue CSV codec: parse, coerce, validate, serialise

Implementation half of the weapons-CSV epic (parent AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7).

## Goal

Extend the existing RFC 4180 codec (`src/core/csv.ts`) with a typed weapon-catalogue codec, in the same style as `coerceEnemyConfig` / `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`. No new dependency; no duplicated CSV parsing logic.

## Deliverables

- `WEAPON_COLUMN_ORDER: (keyof WeaponRow)[]` — stable column contract, exported (like `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`) so the Vite plugin can validate headers.
- `WeaponRow` type — the flat, scalar projection of `WeaponDefinition`:
  `id, name, description, subdivisions, bulletColor, bulletShape, bulletSize, bulletLifetime, bulletShapeLength, bulletRim, bulletThickness, bulletTrail, bulletFlame, maxHitPoints, bounce, splits, orbitPods, orbitRadius, aoeTrigger, aoeRadius, aoeDamagesEnemies, aoeClearsEnemyBullets, aoeDamage, aoeChains, aoeProjectileSpeed, hitscanLength, hitscanDuration, muzzleColor, muzzleRadius, muzzleDuration, impactColor, impactRadius, impactDuration, impactCue`
- `parseWeaponPatterns(csv)` — long format `weaponId,index,angleDeg,sideOffsetPx` → `{ offsets, sideOffsets }` per weapon; degrees → radians at the boundary.
- `coerceWeaponRow(row)` — typed coercion; **optional columns stay absent** when blank (`bounce`/`splits`/`maxHitPoints`/`bulletShapeLength`/`bulletRim`/`bulletThickness`/`bulletTrail`/`bulletFlame`/`aoe*`/`orbit*`/`hitscan*`), because the combat core dispatches on presence.
- The Wave Laser's `hitscan` descriptor is carried as the flat pair `hitscanLength` / `hitscanDuration` (both blank for every non-hitscan weapon) so the beam length and visible duration stay designer-tunable and the wave laser round-trips through the CSV without a special case.
- `validateWeaponRow(row)` — rejects bad enums (`bulletShape`, `aoeTrigger`), non-hex colours, non-finite/negative numbers, unknown weapon ids, duplicate ids; returns a diagnostic naming the row and column.
- `parseWeaponCatalogue(weaponsCsv, patternsCsv): { catalogue, errors }` — merges both files; a row that fails validation falls back to the code default for that id with the diagnostic recorded (never throws).
- `serializeWeaponCatalogue(catalogue)` → `{ weaponsCsv, patternsCsv }` with the documented header comment block (column docs, `0xRRGGBB` note, degrees note), matching the `enemy-configs.csv` comment style.
- `fireRateMs` is **derived** from `subdivisions` through `beatSubdivisionMs` (`src/utils/beat.ts`), never stored — so the on-beat-grid invariant holds by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The tests in child 1 pass.
2. Round-trip: `serializeWeaponCatalogue(parseWeaponCatalogue(x).catalogue)` re-parses to a deeply equal catalogue.
3. Every validation failure produces an actionable diagnostic (id + column + reason); malformed input never throws at the boundary.
4. Absent vs `0` semantics preserved for presence-dispatched fields (asserted).
5. `npm run typecheck` and the changed-scope tests pass; no behaviour change to `enemy-configs.csv` / `ship-config.csv` parsing (their tests stay green).

## Key files

- `src/core/csv.ts` (extend)
- `src/utils/beat.ts` (read-only: `beatSubdivisionMs`)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` (types: `WeaponDefinition`, `BulletShape`, `OrbitDescriptor`, `AoEDescriptor`)

## Depends on

Child 1 (tests).

# Load the weapon catalogue from CSV (runtime source of truth + code fallback)

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Make the parsed CSV the runtime source of truth for `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, with the TypeScript catalogue demoted to a fallback — following the established ladder used for `enemy-configs.csv` and `ship-config.csv`.

## Deliverables

- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — add `?raw` imports for `../data/weapons.csv` and `../data/weapon-patterns.csv`, exported alongside the existing bundled CSVs so the Vite build inlines them (production stays read-only, no runtime fetch).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — rename the current literal to `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (internal fallback, still the authoritative shape/type reference) and expose `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` **built at module load** from `parseWeaponCatalogue(bundledWeaponsCsv, bundledWeaponPatternsCsv).catalogue`, falling back per-weapon to `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE` when a row is missing/invalid.
- `WEAPON_IDS: readonly WeaponId[]` — an explicit runtime id list (replacing reliance on `Record` key exhaustiveness), derived from the fallback catalogue so adding a weapon to the fallback keeps TS exhaustive.
- Boot-time self-check: a dev-only `console.warn` (or a diagnostic surfaced in the gym) listing any id that resolved from fallback instead of CSV, so a typo is visible rather than silent.
- Cadence ownership note in the module header (and on the `subdivisions`/`fireRateMs` fields): the catalogue value is the **legacy nominal** interval used for level-stat quantisation and the hold-full ghost metronome; the **live** cadence is `src/data/weapon-levels.json` (`resolveWeaponPattern`). A dev-only diagnostic warns when `subdivisions` disagrees with the ladder's level-0 rung density, naming `weapon-levels.json` as the cadence source.
- `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` is **derived from the parsed catalogue** (`subdivisions` column) instead of a second hand-maintained literal, and `DEFAULT_RULES.weaponSubdivisions` seeds from it (`src/core/rules.ts`), so a designer's CSV fire-rate edit is not silently overridden by a stale code default. A persisted user override in the rules store still wins at runtime and is documented as a local, uncommitted setting.
- `getWeaponById` / `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` / `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` keep their signatures — the 16 non-test consumers (`Player.ts`, `weaponLevels.ts`, `dropLayer.ts`, `dropDescriptions.ts`, `gymHelp.ts`, `captureCycle.ts`, `GymRhythm.ts`) are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The parsed CSV is the single source of truth for runtime catalogue reads: editing `src/data/weapons.csv` or `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv` (e.g. `cannon` `bulletColor`) and refreshing `npm run dev` changes the live game with **no** TypeScript edit — demonstrated in the work-item comment.
2. `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` is populated from the CSV: a test asserts the runtime value differs from `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE` when the CSV is edited (mocked bundled import), and equals it for the committed seed.
3. A missing/invalid row falls back to the code default for that id only, leaving the remaining weapons CSV-driven.
4. `WEAPON_IDS` covers all 16 ids and `getWeaponById` throws/falls back identically for unknown ids as before.
5. No consumer file needs a change (assert by `git diff --stat`); typecheck clean, no behaviour change to any weapon (`resolveWeaponDefinition` output identical for level 0).
6. `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` and `DEFAULT_RULES.weaponSubdivisions` are asserted equal to the catalogue's `subdivisions` for all 16 weapons, and a test proves editing the bundled CSV changes the derived default table (no second literal to drift).
7. The divergence diagnostic is tested both ways: silent when `subdivisions` matches the ladder's level-0 density (10 weapons), and a named warning for each of the six superposition weapons where the ladder is deliberate (cannon, rapid, arc, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug) — asserted without changing gameplay.
6. Existing roster/doc-guard tests (`weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `weaponFeelRoster.test.ts`, `powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) still pass unchanged, or are updated only to read the resolver rather than a literal.

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts`
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` (verification only)

Children 2 and 3.

# Runtime invariant guards for the data-driven weapon catalogue

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Replace the invariants that were previously guaranteed by the type system and by docs-guard tests with **runtime/data validation**, so a hand edit to the CSV cannot produce a silently broken roster.

## Deliverables

- `validateWeaponCatalogue(catalogue)` (in `src/core/csv.ts` or a `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts` leaf module) enforcing, per weapon and across the roster:
  - **on-beat grid:** every `fireRateMs` satisfies `isOnBeatGrid` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`), i.e. is an exact beat subdivision/multiple at the configured BPM;
  - **unique bullet-shape family:** no two weapons resolve the same canonical shape (`canonicalShape` collapsing the `circle`/`disc` alias), preserving the "every weapon is visually unique" roster guarantee;
  - **unique bullet colour** per weapon;
  - **sane magnitudes:** `bulletSize > 0`, `bulletLifetime > 0`, `aoeRadius >= 0`, `orbitRadius > 0` when `orbitPods` present, `bulletRim`/`impactColor`/`muzzleColor` in `0x000000–0xffffff`;
  - **structural coherence:** `aoeTrigger` present ⇒ `aoeRadius` present; `orbitPods` present ⇒ `orbitRadius` present; `splits`/`bounce`/`maxHitPoints` absent rather than `0` unless intentionally degenerate (flag with a warning).
- Wiring: the guard runs at catalogue build time (dev: surfaces diagnostics; prod: falls back to the code default for offending weapons) and is asserted directly by the test suite.
- Tests: one failing case per invariant (duplicate colour, duplicate shape family, off-beat rate, negative size, missing companion field), each asserting the diagnostic names the weapon id and the field.
- Update the existing docs-guard tests to assert against the parsed catalogue rather than the literal, so the same guarantee is checked for data edits.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Each invariant has at least one negative test proving the guard rejects it, and one positive test proving the committed seed passes.
2. An off-beat `fireRateMs` (e.g. from a hand-edited `subdivisions` of `1.37`) is rejected with a message that states the nearest on-grid value.
3. A duplicate colour/shape edit is rejected with both offending ids named.
4. Diagnostics are surfaced in dev (console/gym status) and never crash boot.
5. `weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts` and `weaponFeelRoster.test.ts` pass against the data-driven catalogue.
6. Malformed rows, unknown columns, invalid enums, off-beat fire rates, duplicate colours/shapes and out-of-range numbers are rejected with a diagnostic or fall back to the code default, and the game still boots.

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` (`isOnBeatGrid`, `canonicalShape`, `BULLET_COLORS`)
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` (canonical shape helper)
- `src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/weaponFeelRoster.test.ts` (update)

## Depends on

Child 4 (catalogue resolved from data).

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

# Weapon tuning panel: sliders + Save / Save As → CSV re-read

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Give designers a no-editor way to retune the values this epic exists for — **fire rate, colours, bullet sizes, AoE radii, impact cues** — with live preview, following the `GymBotTuning` panel precedent (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` + `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`).

## Deliverables

- A new gym scene `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponTuning.ts` (registered in the gym index alongside the other tuning gyms) with:
  - a weapon selector over `WEAPON_IDS` (16 entries), showing the resolved definition;
  - live-editable controls for the goal fields: `bulletColor`, `bulletSize`, `bulletLifetime`, `bulletShape` (+ rim/trail/thickness/flame), `aoeRadius`/`aoeTrigger` for the AOE family, `orbitRadius`/`orbitPods` for Options, and `impactColor`/`impactRadius`/`impactDuration`/`impactCue`;
  - a **rhythm panel** (not a fire-rate slider): the selected weapon's ladder rendered from `WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDERS` as level → rung (`k`, `n`, `rotation`, onsets/beat, derived interval), with a read-only preview that fires the selected rung on a dummy target so its shape is audible and visible. Editing rhythm is a hand-edit of `src/data/weapon-levels.json` in this epic (no write path; a Save for rhythm is a follow-up), and the panel states that plainly. A read-only **nominal subdivision** figure is derived from the active rung so designers can see the legacy `subdivisions` comparison without being offered a control that would not change cadence;
  - live preview firing the selected weapon on a dummy target so colour/size/impact changes are visible immediately;
  - **Save** (upsert the current row) and **Save As** (duplicate under a new id, refused unless a fallback/icon/cue path exists, per child 6) writing through the dev plugin then **re-reading** the CSV so the running catalogue updates;
  - a status line showing the endpoint result (saved / rejected with reason / read-only build).
- Production/static behaviour: writes disabled with a clear status message; values still load read-only from the bundled CSV.
- Tests (`src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponTuning.test.ts`): control binding to the resolved definition, Save builds the expected PUT payload, Save-As sanitises and rejects duplicates, re-read updates the scene's catalogue view, and read-only mode disables Save.

5. The panel is discoverable from the gym index and documented in the gym listing.
6. Every control is keyboard-accessible and follows the existing panel conventions (no bespoke widget styles).

# Integration: designer round-trip + production read-only

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Prove the end-to-end loop a designer will actually use, and prove the shipped build stays safe and read-only.

## Deliverables

An integration test suite covering:

1. **Hand-edit round-trip:** start from the committed CSVs, edit `bulletColor` + `subdivisions` + `aoeRadius` in a fixture copy, reload the catalogue, and assert the resolved `WeaponDefinition`s reflect the edit and that `resolveWeaponDefinition(id, 0)` returns the edited base.
2. **Panel round-trip:** PUT via the dev plugin (temp dir) → catalogue re-read → resolved definition reflects the write; the second read is a no-op.
2b. **Ladder round-trip:** edit one weapon's level-0 rung in a fixture copy of `src/data/weapon-levels.json`, reload, and assert `resolveWeaponPattern(id, level)` returns the edited rhythm for that weapon while every other weapon's ladder is unchanged; a malformed ladder falls back to the code ladder with a diagnostic and boot still succeeds.
3. **Fallback path:** a corrupted/invalid row (bad colour, off-beat subdivision) → that weapon resolves from `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, every other weapon stays CSV-driven, boot succeeds, diagnostics recorded.
4. **Production path:** with the dev plugin absent, the bundled CSV is used, writes are refused/disabled and no network call is attempted.
5. **Parity in-game:** the game and every gym that renders a player weapon (`PlayScene`, `GymWeapons`, `GymRhythm`, `GymWeaponLeveling`) show the same colour/size/impact for the edited weapon — the gym↔game parity rule (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) holds for data-driven values.
6. **No behavioural regression:** a frozen snapshot test asserts every weapon's level-0 and level-3 resolved definition is unchanged by the migration (guarding `weaponLevels.resolveWeaponDefinition` interplay).

## Acceptance criteria

1. All six scenarios are automated and green, with meaningful assertions (no presence-only checks).
2. Scenario 4 asserts no fetch is attempted in production mode (stubbed fetch, zero calls).
3. Scenario 5 asserts identical resolved visual/impact specs and identical fire rhythms between `PlayScene` and the gyms — not merely that both scenes boot.
4. UK English throughout, and the full suite passes (`/skill:test`), with `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` clean; all tests from previous epics still pass, so the epic is done only when children 1–9 are closed and this suite is green.

# Docs: weapons CSV schema, retuning guide, invariants

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Document the new designer workflow so retuning weapons needs no engineer and no archaeology, and so the invariants that used to be compiler-enforced are written down.

## Deliverables

- `docs/BALANCING.md` — new section "Weapon tuning CSV (AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7)":
  - where the files are (`src/data/weapons.csv`, `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv`) and what each column means (table mirroring the header comment);
  - the designer workflow (hand-edit → refresh; or panel → Save), and that a **rebuild is required for production** while dev reflects changes on refresh;
  - the "blank means absent" convention and why (`bounce`/`splits`/`maxHitPoints`/`aoe*`/`orbit*` presence drives dispatch);
  - angles authored in degrees, radians internally;
  - fire rate is authored as **shots per beat** and must stay on the beat grid (link to the beat-grid section already in that doc);
  - the invariants (unique shape family, unique colour, on-beat rates) and that they are runtime-validated with fallback to code defaults;
  - what a CSV row **cannot** do: add a weapon (needs an icon in `icons.ts` and a cue in `effects.ts`) or change the level ladder.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — extend the existing "Weapon Euclidean upgrade ladder" section: the ladders now live in `src/data/weapon-levels.json`; document the file shape (`weaponId` → ordered rungs of `{ k, n, rotation }`), the 16th-note lattice and derived step, how `minLevel` thresholds are derived from the `fireRate` curve, the fallback/precedence ladder, and that **this file, not `weapons.csv` `subdivisions`, is the live cadence**.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — note that the weapon panel is a tuning surface, not a gameplay gym, and that data-driven values must not diverge between `PlayScene` and the gyms.
- Code comments: `src/utils/weapons.ts` header explains the fallback ladder (`CSV → DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE → per-weapon fallback`); `src/core/csv.ts` weapon codec section documents `WEAPON_COLUMN_ORDER` and the degrees/absent conventions.
- `README.md` — one-line pointer under the configuration section if it lists the CSV files today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A designer who has never seen the repo can follow the doc to change a bullet colour, a fire rate and a Nova AoE radius, including how to verify the change.
2. Every column of `weapons.csv` appears in the table with units and legal values.
3. The doc states explicitly what each surface can and cannot do: `weapons.csv` cannot add a weapon (needs an icon in `icons.ts` and a cue in `effects.ts`), cannot change cadence (that is `weapon-levels.json`), and `weapon-levels.json` cannot add a weapon either — with the follow-up path for each stated.
4. Docs assertions in the docs-guard tests (if they inspect `docs/BALANCING.md`) remain green, or are extended to cover the new section.
5. UK English, no broken relative links, no CHANGELOG entry (excluded by project policy).
6. The CSV schema, the retuning workflow, the invariants and the read-only production behaviour are documented in `docs/BALANCING.md` (plus the `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` touch-point) and reflected in code comments where the catalogue is consumed.

## Implementation complete — commit 172ff209 (pushed to dev)

### What landed

`src/core/csv.ts` now carries the weapon-catalogue codec (a new `// ── Weapon catalogue codec ──` section, ~950 lines with docs):

- `WEAPON_COLUMN_ORDER` (34 columns, exactly the contract order) + `WEAPON_PATTERN_COLUMN_ORDER`.
- `WeaponRow` (flat projection; no `fireRateMs`, no pattern arrays).
- `WEAPON_IDS` — the runtime id roster, declared in the codec because `parseWeaponPatterns` is used standalone and `src/utils/weapons.ts` imports this module (a value back-import would be a cycle). Typed `Record<WeaponId, true>`, so roster/union drift is a compile error.
- `coerceWeaponRow` — blank optional cells stay **absent** (an explicit `0` stays `0`).
- `validateWeaponRow` — one pass, flat diagnostics `<id>: <column>: <reason>`; required columns, enums (`bulletShape`, `aoeTrigger`), `0xRRGGBB` colours, finite/positive/negative rules, boolean format, unknown ids, and descriptor-group completeness.
- `parseWeaponPatterns` — degrees→radians at the boundary, ordered by `index`, unknown ids and NaN angles rejected.
- `parseWeaponCatalogue` — merges both files, derives `fireRateMs` via `beatSubdivisionMs`, omits invalid rows and records diagnostics, first definition wins on duplicate ids, never throws.
- `serializeWeaponCatalogue` — documented header comment blocks (column docs, `0xRRGGBB`, degrees, blank-means-absent), colours as `0xRRGGBB`, angles in degrees to 3 dp, `subdivisions` derived back from `fireRateMs`, one pattern row per bullet.

### Decisions worth reviewing

1. **Descriptor groups are declared by their opening column** (`orbitPods`, `aoeTrigger`, `hitscanLength`, `impactColor`): the opener present but blank with every other group cell blank is an absent group (so a header may list a group's columns without any weapon using it); an opener absent while another group column is declared is a diagnostic (a member must never be silently dropped).
2. **The muzzle flash is always present.** The committed contract tests require a row with only `muzzleColor` (and even a row with no muzzle columns) to yield a `muzzleFlash`; it therefore defaults to `{ color: bulletColor, radius: 7, duration: 0.12 }` (the shared `MUZZLE_FLASH_*` defaults, declared in the codec to avoid importing a VFX module). Every shipped weapon already carries an explicit flash, so the frozen-fixture round-trip is exact; a synthetic definition *without* a flash would re-parse with the defaulted one (documented on `serializeWeaponCatalogue`).
3. AOE/orbit/hitscan/impact stay all-or-nothing: their required members have no meaningful default.

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm run build` — clean (incl. bundle hygiene).
- Full suite on the pushed tree (`npm --silent test`, run through the test skill): **429 files / 9728 tests passed, 1 skipped** (the skipped one is `weaponCatalogueParity.test.ts`'s seed-file assertion, which activates with child 3). The child-1 codec suites are now active (43 tests) and green.
- The dev-push hook reported `full-suite=no-evidence` for this push (the repo's pre-push hook did not leave a cache entry); the full suite was run manually afterwards against clean commit 172ff209 and is green.
